caption:
Google is rolling out Tasks in Gemini, its AI agent, for free in six countries, including the US.
In the US it can call businesses for you, log in to sites and check out with Google Pay.
You can set a hard spending cap, and Google says nothing is bought until you approve it.

Would you let an AI agent spend your money?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Android Police, Unite.AI · Photo: Android Police
threads_text: Google just made its Gemini agent free in six countries, and in the US it can call businesses and pay with Google Pay for you. Until now this was for paid subscribers only. Would you let an AI agent make purchases for you?

slides.headline: Google just made its Gemini AI agent *free*, and it can call businesses and pay for you

slides.heading: Free in *six countries*
paras: Tasks in Gemini used to be for paid Pro and Ultra subscribers. Now it is rolling out free to adults in the US, Canada, Australia, India, Japan and South Korea.
It runs on Gemini 4 Hydrogen. Google says it reaches hundreds of millions of people.

slides.heading: It *calls businesses* for you
paras: In the US, Gemini can phone local businesses and book restaurants, hotels or appointments, then add them to your Google Calendar.
It says it is an AI on the call, and businesses can opt out.
slides.note: Calling is not available in IN, LA, MN, MT and NE.

slides.heading: It can *buy things*, with a cap
paras: Gemini can check out with Google Pay on Visa and Mastercard. You can set a hard spending cap first.

paras.t: Google says nothing is bought until you approve it.

slides.heading: Text it or *email it*
paras: US users can also text Gemini or forward an email to gemini@google.com with instructions.
Google warns tasks can still fail, and some sites hand the last click back to you.

slides.hook: Follow to see what free AI agents can really do for you, and where they still fail.

site_article.headline: Google makes Tasks in Gemini free in six countries and adds calls and payments in the US
site_article.dek: The agent, once limited to paying subscribers, now runs on Gemini 4 Hydrogen and can phone businesses, log in to sites and check out with Google Pay for US users.
site_article.summary: Google is rolling out Tasks in Gemini, its personal AI agent, for free to adults in the US, Canada, Australia, India, Japan and South Korea. In the US the agent can also call businesses, use Google Password Manager and pay with Google Pay under a spending cap the user sets.
site_article.seo_title: Gemini Tasks is now free: calls, Google Pay and limits
site_article.seo_description: Google made Tasks in Gemini free in six countries. What the agent can do, the US-only calling and payment features, the spending cap and the limits.
site_article.answer_summary: Tasks in Gemini is now free for users 18 and older in the US, Canada, Australia, India, Japan and South Korea. Calling businesses, Google Pay checkout, texting and emailing Gemini are available only in the US for now.
site_article.hero_alt: A Google Pixel phone showing the Gemini app start screen with the Task option.

paragraphs.text: Google announced on November 17, 2026 that Tasks in Gemini, the personal AI agent inside the Gemini app, is rolling out for free in six countries, according to Unite.AI and Android Police. Free access covers users 18 and older in the United States, Canada, Australia, India, Japan and South Korea, and Google says the rollout reaches hundreds of millions of people.

The feature was previously called Spark and was limited to paying Pro and Ultra subscribers, Android Police reported. Google introduced Gemini Spark on May 19, 2026 as a cloud based agent running on Gemini 3.5. Tasks now runs on Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the fast model Google released on November 12, 2026 for agent work.

Users reach the agent by switching the control on the Gemini home screen from Chat to Tasks, on the web or in the mobile app. The agent can keep working in the background and notify the user when results are ready, according to Unite.AI.
Calls, logins and payments in the US

A set of advanced features starts in the US only. Gemini can call local businesses, sign in to websites through Google Password Manager without the user sharing passwords, compare products and check out with Google Pay. Android Police reported that the agent can book hotel, restaurant and service appointments, check Google Calendar for a free time and add the booking to the calendar.

Google says Gemini tells businesses it is an AI when it calls, and businesses can opt out of these calls. Calling is not available in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana and Nebraska, according to Unite.AI and Data Studios.

Purchases use the Agent Payments Protocol with tokens from Visa and Mastercard on supported cards, and users can set a hard spending cap in advance. Data Studios reported that Gemini prepares the checkout, sends an itemized summary and buys nothing without one tap approval, using a single use virtual card from Google Pay. Receipts go to Google Wallet. American Express support is listed as coming soon.

US users can also assign work by forwarding an email to gemini@google.com or by texting Gemini after verifying a US phone number on an eligible carrier. Data Studios said the payment, text and email features require personal Google accounts and English. Gemini connects natively with Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, YouTube and Maps.

Google says each user's tasks run in a dedicated, hardware isolated virtual machine on Google Cloud's Agent Compute Engine, with prompt injection filters and Safe Browsing limiting what the agent can open. Gemini asks for confirmation before purchases and other critical steps, and third party connections are off by default, Unite.AI reported. Data Studios noted that Google has not published independent test results for these protections.

Google also cautions that tasks can fail or miss their goal, and that on some websites Gemini hands the screen back to the user for the final click. Data Studios pointed out that Google has not stated usage limits for free users, including for tasks, calls or purchases.

Moving the agent from a paid beta to a free feature turns AI agents from a demo for subscribers into something ordinary phone users will try. The calling and payment tools are the parts that touch real money and real businesses, which is why Google is starting them in one country and wrapping them in caps and confirmations.
The next thing to watch is whether Google publishes usage limits for free users and brings calling and payments to the five other countries.
